mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions for corporations and households.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: In a rising rate cycle, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05), or the 5-day realized volatility of SPX is lower than historical averages during the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by at least 0.2 percentage points predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as labor market strength supports corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10,000 and UNRATE decreases by ≥0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window, the SPX 20-day forward return is negative despite the labor indicators meeting or exceeding the trigger, or the correlation between the indicators and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 5.0% followed within two months by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as a contrarian signal of weakening demand for durable goods.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥5.0% in one month and rebounds in the following month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such trigger periods, or the pattern recurs more than twice in a 12-month window without positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative as investors anticipate the Federal Reserve will raise rates to curb inflation, reducing equity valuations.
failure_condition: During such inflation spikes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the S&P 500 outperforms a risk-free rate proxy by more than 1.5 percentage points over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) by at least 10% for three consecutive months indicates a cooling housing market, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as credit expansion for the housing sector tightens.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥10% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during such periods, or the decline in HOUST reverses before the 60-day window closes.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both unemployment insurance claims (PAYEMS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 5% in the same month signal a labor market adjustment, leading to a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as risk aversion is reduced.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥5% and CPIAUCSL increases by ≥5% in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such co-movement, or the interaction effect is not significant in a two-variable regression (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp and unexpected decline in consumer confidence (measured by a proxy such as UNRATE turning negative for the first time in three months) predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as market participants anticipate easing tightening constraints on corporate lending.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 0.0% for the first time in three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such confidence shocks, or the effect is only observed in recessionary macro regimes (as classified by NFP data).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4.0%, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days is expected to be positive as the market anticipates a sustained easing cycle and lower borrowing costs for equities.
failure_condition: During periods meeting the trigger, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is not robust across multiple central bank policy rate cuts (>2 instances in 12 months).
